cands.name: Amy Trask
cands.bio: Democrat, 33. Homeschooling parent who does occasional freelance editing and civic work; says she is a seventh-generation Floridian with roots in LaBelle. Lost the 2024 Democratic primary for this seat to David Arreola. Has not held elected office.
cands.local_ties: Files from Alachua County per FL DOE; describes family roots in LaBelle (News4JAX guide). Her specific home town was not stated in sources found.

record.text: Has never held elected office; ran in the 2024 Democratic primary for HD 22 against David Arreola.

Campaign says she has drafted bills including a "HAVEN Act". The News4JAX guide says one became law; a Sept 2025 GNV Info article says the HAVEN Act did not pass. These accounts conflict and are unverified.

endorsements.text: Gainesville City Commissioner James Ingle and Pride Community Center board member Joe Smith (as reported at her Sept 2025 launch).

cands.gaps: Sources conflict on whether a bill she drafted became law and on a 2022 run; only the 2024 primary is confirmed here. No usable photo found. Owner-source check was limited: the alexjoneslive.com site search was run for this name and returned no results. stewpeters.com, rumble.com and infowars.com searches were blocked (HTTP 403) and the shared web-search quota was exhausted, so those were NOT checked.

cands.name: Chad Johnson
cands.bio: Republican incumbent. Auctioneer and sales manager; former Levy County Commissioner (2009-2014); former president of the Levy County Farm Bureau and the Florida Auctioneers Association. UF B.S. in agricultural economics. Elected to HD 22 in 2024.
cands.local_ties: Born in Gainesville (Wikipedia); filed from Levy County; former Levy County commissioner.

record.text: Levy County Commissioner 2009-2014; HD 22 representative since Nov 2024, succeeding Chuck Clemons.
Says he received an Associated Industries of Florida "Champion Legislator" award (self-reported in the News4JAX guide).

endorsements.text: Outgoing Rep. Chuck Clemons endorsed him in the 2024 open-seat race.

cands.gaps: Donors, committees and 2026 endorsements not found. Owner-source check was limited: the alexjoneslive.com site search was run for this name and returned no results. stewpeters.com, rumble.com and infowars.com searches were blocked (HTTP 403) and the shared web-search quota was exhausted, so those were NOT checked.

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.
The 2025-26 General Appropriations Act (state budget), final vote.
Immigration enforcement bill from the 2025 special session: state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Post-hurricane emergency management bill that also limits local governments' ability to adopt stricter development rules after storms.

second-amendment.evidence: Voted Yea on HB 133 (2026), which repeals the 2018 law that raised the long-gun purchase age to 21 (passed the House 74-37 on 01/15/2026).

pro-life.evidence: Voted Yea on CS/HB 289 (2026, House 76-34 on 01/15/2026); also voted Yea on its 2025 predecessor CS/HB 1517 (79-32 on 04/09/2025). The bill lets parents sue for the wrongful death of an unborn child and bars suits against the mother or against providers of lawful medical care, so it does not itself restrict abortion; abortion-rights groups opposed it.
